Chennai.name: Marina Beach
Chennai.blurb: Marina Beach is a natural urban beach in Chennai along the Bay of Bengal, stretching over 12 km.
Chennai.bestThing: Walking along India's longest natural urban beach at sunrise.

Chennai.name: Kapaleeshwarar Temple
Chennai.blurb: A 7th-century Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, built in classic Dravidian architectural style with a gopuram.
Chennai.bestThing: Admiring the colorful 37-meter rainbow gopuram and temple tank.

Chennai.name: Fort St. George
Chennai.blurb: Founded in 1644, Fort St. George is the first English fortress in India, now housing the Fort Museum and St. Mary's Church.
Chennai.bestThing: Exploring British East India Company relics and St. Mary's Church.

Chennai.name: St. Thomas Cathedral Basilica
Chennai.blurb: A minor basilica built by Portuguese explorers in the 16th century over the tomb of Saint Thomas the Apostle.
Chennai.bestThing: Visiting the underground tomb chamber of St. Thomas.

Chennai.name: Government Museum
Chennai.blurb: Established in 1851, it is the second oldest museum in India, famous for its Bronze Gallery of Chola bronzes.
Chennai.bestThing: Viewing world-renowned 10th-century Chola Bronze statues.

Chennai.name: Valluvar Kottam
Chennai.blurb: A modern monument dedicated to the ancient Tamil poet-philosopher Thiruvalluvar, shaped like a giant temple chariot.
Chennai.bestThing: Seeing all 1,330 Thirukkural verses engraved on granite pillars.

Chennai.name: Guindy National Park
Chennai.blurb: One of the few national parks situated inside a major Indian city, home to blackbucks, spotted deer, and jackals.
Chennai.bestThing: Spotting wild blackbucks and rare birds in urban green woods.

Chennai.name: Edward Elliot's Beach
Chennai.blurb: Popularly known as Bessie Beach, a clean and relaxed coastal promenade featuring the Karl Schmidt Memorial.
Chennai.bestThing: Unwinding near the Karl Schmidt Memorial with coastal snacks.

Chennai.name: DakshinaChitra
Chennai.blurb: A living-history heritage museum showcasing 18 authentic reconstructed historic houses of South India.
Chennai.bestThing: Walking through real traditional timber houses from 4 southern states.

Chennai.name: Arignar Anna Zoological Park
Chennai.blurb: Also known as Vandalur Zoo, it spans 1,490 acres and is one of the largest zoological parks in Southeast Asia.
Chennai.bestThing: Taking the lion & deer safari across vast natural enclosures.

Chennai.name: Parthasarathy Temple
Chennai.blurb: An 8th-century Vaishnavite temple built by the Pallavas, dedicated to Lord Krishna as Parthasarathy.
Chennai.bestThing: Viewing the ancient Pallava stone inscriptions and ornate Gopuram.

Chennai.name: Birla Planetarium
Chennai.blurb: Part of the Periyar Science and Technology Centre, featuring automated sky shows and astronomy exhibits.
Chennai.bestThing: Watching 360-degree cosmic projection shows inside the dome.

Chennai.name: Connemara Public Library
Chennai.blurb: Established in 1896, it is one of India's four National Depository Libraries with rare century-old volumes.
Chennai.bestThing: Marveling at Victorian oak-carved reading rooms and antique books.

Chennai.name: Ripon Building
Chennai.blurb: An iconic neoclassical white building built in 1913, serving as the headquarters of the Greater Chennai Corporation.
Chennai.bestThing: Photographing the majestic white Greco-Roman architecture.

Chennai.name: Ashtalakshmi Temple
Chennai.blurb: A multi-tiered coastal temple dedicated to goddess Lakshmi in eight forms, located right on Elliot's Beach shore.
Chennai.bestThing: Ascending the multi-level shrine with ocean waves in the background.

Chennai.name: Vadapalani Murugan Temple
Chennai.blurb: A major Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Murugan, built in the late 19th century and renowned for weddings.
Chennai.bestThing: Experiencing vibrant daily rituals and colorful Rajagopuram.

Chennai.name: Semmozhi Poonga
Chennai.blurb: A 20-acre botanical garden in the city center featuring over 500 species of exotic plants and a vertical garden.
Chennai.bestThing: Strolling past peaceful lily ponds and curated fern gardens.

Chennai.name: Kalakshetra Foundation
Chennai.blurb: Founded in 1936 by Rukmini Devi Arundale, an internationally renowned academy for Bharatanatyam dance and music.
Chennai.bestThing: Walking through serene banyan-shaded open-air art classrooms.

Chennai.name: T. Nagar Ranganathan Street
Chennai.blurb: One of the most crowded and famous commercial shopping streets in Asia, known for silks, gold, and apparel.
Chennai.bestThing: Immersing in the high-energy shopping crowd for traditional silk sarees.

Chennai.name: Cholamandal Artists' Village
Chennai.blurb: India's largest artists' commune founded in 1966, displaying contemporary paintings and outdoor sculptures.
Chennai.bestThing: Viewing open-air contemporary bronze and granite sculptures.

Chennai.name: Express Avenue Mall
Chennai.blurb: A premier retail destination built on 8 acres in Royapettah with over 200 stores and gaming centers.
Chennai.bestThing: Enjoying modern shopping, dining, and indoor entertainment.

Chennai.name: Chetpet Eco Park
Chennai.blurb: A 16-acre urban lake park featuring walking trails, angling facilities, and boating in central Chennai.
Chennai.bestThing: Boating on the serene lake right in the middle of Chetpet.

Chennai.name: Madras Crocodile Bank Trust
Chennai.blurb: A herpetological research station founded by Romulus Whitaker, home to thousands of crocodiles, alligators, and turtles.
Chennai.bestThing: Watching daytime crocodile feedings and venom extraction demos.

Chennai.name: Government Museum Art Gallery
Chennai.blurb: Housed inside the National Art Gallery building in Egmore, showcasing Mughal miniatures and Raja Ravi Varma paintings.
Chennai.bestThing: Admiring rare original portrait paintings by Raja Ravi Varma.

Chennai.name: Marundeeswarar Temple
Chennai.blurb: A Chola-era temple dedicated to Lord Shiva as the divine healer, famous for its grand gateway and medicinal folklore.
Chennai.bestThing: Experiencing peaceful Chola-era courtyard shrines and holy water tank.

Delhi.name: Qutub Minar
Delhi.blurb: A 73-meter UNESCO World Heritage brick minaret built in 1192 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, featuring intricate Arabic inscriptions.
Delhi.bestThing: Standing beneath the world's tallest brick minaret and ancient Iron Pillar.

Delhi.name: Red Fort
Delhi.blurb: Constructed in 1639 by Emperor Shah Jahan in red sandstone, serving as the main seat of the Mughal Empire.
Delhi.bestThing: Walking through Diwan-i-Aam and Lahori Gate where history unfolded.

Delhi.name: Humayun's Tomb
Delhi.blurb: A UNESCO site built in 1570, it is the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent and inspired the Taj Mahal.
Delhi.bestThing: Marveling at red sandstone Persian charbagh garden architecture.
Delhi.nearTransport: Jor Bagh Metro / JLN Stadium Metro

Delhi.name: India Gate
Delhi.blurb: A 42-meter high war memorial arch built in 1931 honoring 84,000 soldiers of the British Indian Army.
Delhi.bestThing: Strolling along Kartavya Path while India Gate glows illuminated at night.

Delhi.name: Jama Masjid
Delhi.blurb: Built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan between 1644 and 1656, one of India's largest congregational mosques.
Delhi.bestThing: Climbing the southern minaret for breathtaking panoramic views of Old Delhi.

Delhi.name: Lotus Temple
Delhi.blurb: A Bahá'í House of Worship shaped like a lotus flower with 27 free-standing marble petals, open to all faiths.
Delhi.bestThing: Experiencing complete quiet meditation inside the sunlit white marble hall.

Delhi.name: Akshardham Temple
Delhi.blurb: A massive Hindu temple complex carved from pink sandstone and marble, showcasing traditional Indian art and heritage.
Delhi.bestThing: Watching the Sahaj Anand water and laser light show after sunset.

Delhi.name: Rashtrapati Bhavan
Delhi.blurb: The official residence of the President of India, designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens and completed in 1929.
Delhi.bestThing: Viewing the 340-room grand palace and the seasonal Mughal Gardens.

Delhi.name: Jantar Mantar
Delhi.blurb: An astronomical observatory erected in 1724 by Maharaja Jai Singh II of Jaipur, housing 13 stone instruments.
Delhi.bestThing: Inspecting the massive Samrat Yantra sundial accurately measuring time.

Delhi.name: Chandni Chowk
Delhi.blurb: One of India's oldest and busiest wholesale markets, established in the 17th century by Shah Jahan's daughter Jahanara.
Delhi.bestThing: Sampling legendary Paranthe Wali Gali flatbreads and street sweets.

Delhi.name: Lodhi Garden
Delhi.blurb: A 90-acre city park containing tombs of 15th-century Sayyid and Lodhi rulers amidst lush lawns and trees.
Delhi.bestThing: Walking past 500-year-old medieval tombs surrounded by blooming flowers.

Delhi.name: National Museum
Delhi.blurb: Established in 1949, housing over 200,000 works of art spanning 5,000 years, including Harappan artifacts.
Delhi.bestThing: Viewing the famous bronze 'Dancing Girl' statue from Mohenjo-daro.

Delhi.name: Purana Qila
Delhi.blurb: One of the oldest forts in Delhi, rebuilt by Sher Shah Suri and Emperor Humayun on the ancient mound of Indraprastha.
Delhi.bestThing: Exploring the Sher Mandal octagonal library tower and lakeside lawns.
Delhi.nearTransport: Pragati Maidan Metro / Supreme Court Metro

Delhi.name: Agrasen ki Baoli
Delhi.blurb: A 60-meter long historical stepwell consisting of 108 steps across three levels, built in medieval times.
Delhi.bestThing: Descending the stone staircase of Delhi's most picturesque hidden stepwell.

Delhi.name: Raj Ghat
Delhi.blurb: A serene black marble memorial structure marking the spot of Mahatma Gandhi's cremation in 1948.
Delhi.bestThing: Paying silent respects near the eternal flame at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial.

Delhi.name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
Delhi.blurb: One of the most prominent Sikh gurdwaras in Delhi, known for its golden dome and sacred water pool (Sarovar).
Delhi.bestThing: Visiting the holy pool and partaking in the community kitchen (Langar).
Delhi.nearTransport: Patel Chowk Metro / Shivaji Stadium Metro

Delhi.name: Dilli Haat INA
Delhi.blurb: An open-air food plaza and craft bazaar showcasing authentic regional handicrafts and cuisine from all Indian states.
Delhi.bestThing: Tasting authentic regional dishes from Nagaland momos to Rajasthani thalis.

Delhi.name: Safdarjung Tomb
Delhi.area: Air Force Golf Course, Lodhi Road
Delhi.blurb: A sandstone and marble mausoleum built in 1754 for Safdarjung, representing the late Mughal style.
Delhi.bestThing: Admiring the grand domed gateway framing symmetrical gardens.

Delhi.name: Sundar Nursery
Delhi.blurb: A 90-acre heritage park complex adjoining Humayun's Tomb, home to 15 UNESCO-restored Mughal monuments and rare flora.
Delhi.bestThing: Picnicking beside restored Mughal water canals and lotus ponds.

Delhi.name: National Gallery of Modern Art
Delhi.blurb: Housed in the former palace of the Maharaja of Jaipur, exhibiting over 17,000 works of modern Indian art.
Delhi.bestThing: Viewing masterpieces by Amrita Sher-Gil and Rabindranath Tagore.

Delhi.name: Hauz Khas Fort & Lake
Delhi.blurb: A 14th-century medieval complex consisting of a water reservoir, madrasa, tomb, and mosque built during the Delhi Sultanate.
Delhi.bestThing: Watching sunset over the medieval lake from ancient stone pavilion ruins.

Delhi.name: Mehrauli Archaeological Park
Delhi.blurb: Spanning 200 acres, it contains over 100 historically significant monuments spanning 1,000 years of continuous habitation.
Delhi.bestThing: Discovering Jamali Kamali mosque and Rajon ki Baoli stepwell.

Delhi.name: Connaught Place
Delhi.blurb: A major financial and commercial hub built in Georgian architecture with two concentric circles of white colonnaded colonnades.
Delhi.bestThing: Strolling through Inner Circle colonnades and central park flag.

Delhi.name: Crafts Museum
Delhi.blurb: An open-air museum displaying traditional Indian village architecture, folk crafts, and live artisan demonstrations.
Delhi.bestThing: Observing rural artisans crafting pottery, textiles, and wood carvings live.

Delhi.name: Nizamuddin Dargah
Delhi.blurb: The mausoleum of Sufi saint Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya, famous for soul-stirring evening Qawwali music performances.
Delhi.bestThing: Listening to soulful Sufi Qawwali music on Thursday evenings.

Mumbai.name: Gateway of India
Mumbai.blurb: An iconic 26-meter basalt arch monument erected in 1924 to commemorate the landing of King George V and Queen Mary in 1911.
Mumbai.bestThing: Posing with the basalt arch facing the Arabian Sea and Taj Mahal Palace Hotel.

Mumbai.name: Marine Drive
Mumbai.blurb: A 3.6-kilometer C-shaped boulevard along the coast, known as the Queen's Necklace due to evening street lights.
Mumbai.bestThing: Sitting on the promenade tetrapods watching the sunset and glowing arc.

Mumbai.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
Mumbai.blurb: A UNESCO World Heritage Victorian Gothic historic railway station designed by F. W. Stevens and opened in 1887.
Mumbai.bestThing: Admiring Victorian Gothic gargoyles and glowing night illumination.

Mumbai.name: Elephanta Caves
Mumbai.blurb: A UNESCO site of rock-cut cave temples dedicated to Shiva, dating back to the 5th to 8th centuries.
Mumbai.bestThing: Viewing the breathtaking 6-meter Trimurti Sadashiva rock sculpture.

Mumbai.name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya
Mumbai.blurb: Formerly Prince of Wales Museum, displaying 50,000 artifacts in Indo-Saracenic architecture built in 1922.
Mumbai.bestThing: Exploring ancient Indian sculptures, natural history, and miniature art.

Mumbai.name: Sanjay Gandhi National Park
Mumbai.blurb: A 104-sq-km protected forest area within city limits, housing Kanheri rock-cut caves and wild leopards.
Mumbai.bestThing: Riding bicycles through forest trails to 2,000-year-old Kanheri Caves.

Mumbai.name: Kanheri Caves
Mumbai.blurb: A group of 109 Buddhist rock-cut monuments carved into basalt outcrops between 1st century BCE and 10th century CE.
Mumbai.bestThing: Climbing rock stairs to ancient prayer halls and stupas.

Mumbai.name: Haji Ali Dargah
Mumbai.blurb: A 15th-century mosque and tomb built on an islet off the coast of Worli, connected by a narrow causeway.
Mumbai.bestThing: Walking the narrow causeway surrounded by the sea during low tide.

Mumbai.name: Siddhivinayak Temple
Mumbai.blurb: A revered 1801 Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Ganesha, featuring a wooden door carved with images of Ashtavinayak.
Mumbai.bestThing: Joining worship rituals at Mumbai's most iconic Ganesha shrine.

Mumbai.name: Juhu Beach
Mumbai.blurb: One of Mumbai's most celebrated beaches along the Arabian Sea, renowned for street food stalls and sunsets.
Mumbai.bestThing: Eating spicy Pav Bhaji and Bhelpuri right by the tide line.

Mumbai.name: Colaba Causeway
Mumbai.blurb: A bustling commercial street famous for street shopping, antique stalls, trinkets, and legendary cafes.
Mumbai.bestThing: Bargaining for fashion accessories and grabbing coffee at Cafe Leopold.

Mumbai.name: Bandra-Worli Sea Link
Mumbai.blurb: An 8-lane cable-stayed bridge spanning 5.6 km across the open sea, linking Mumbai's western suburbs to South Mumbai.
Mumbai.bestThing: Viewing the illuminated cable bridge from Bandra Fort promenade.
Mumbai.entryCost: Toll ₹85 per car (Free view from promenade)

Mumbai.name: Bandra Fort
Mumbai.blurb: A 1640 Portuguese fort structure perched on a rocky cliff overlooking the sea and Bandra-Worli Sea Link.
Mumbai.bestThing: Catching sea breeze views of the Sea Link from Portuguese stone arches.

Mumbai.name: Bandstand Promenade
Mumbai.blurb: A 1.2-km long coastal walkway featuring the Walk of the Stars and home to celebrity residences like Mannat.
Mumbai.bestThing: Strolling along the rocky coastline past Shah Rukh Khan's Mannat.

Mumbai.name: Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Museum
Mumbai.blurb: Mumbai's oldest museum established in 1855, showcasing city history, industrial arts, and Victorian interiors.
Mumbai.bestThing: Marveling at restored 19th-century gilded Victorian decorative arches.

Mumbai.name: Banganga Tank
Mumbai.blurb: An ancient rectangular freshwater water tank built in 1127 AD by the Silhara dynasty, surrounded by temples.
Mumbai.bestThing: Experiencing ancient temple stairs and tranquil freshwater springs.

Mumbai.name: Hanging Gardens
Mumbai.blurb: Also known as Pherozeshah Mehta Gardens, featuring topiary animal hedges and sunset views over Marine Drive.
Mumbai.bestThing: Watching sunset over Queen's Necklace from Malabar Hill peak.

Mumbai.name: Chor Bazaar
Mumbai.blurb: One of the largest antique and flea markets in India, famous for vintage clocks, brass items, and curiosities.
Mumbai.bestThing: Hunting for antique vinyl records, old gramophones, and brass curios.

Mumbai.name: Crawford Market
Mumbai.blurb: Officially Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Mandai, a historic 1869 market featuring friezes designed by Lockwood Kipling.
Mumbai.bestThing: Viewing historic relief stone carvings above the Norman arch entrance.

Mumbai.name: Flora Fountain
Mumbai.blurb: An intricately carved 1864 Portland stone fountain depicting Roman goddess Flora, located in South Mumbai.
Mumbai.bestThing: Photographing the heritage stone fountain at the heart of South Mumbai.

Mumbai.name: Nehru Science Centre
Mumbai.blurb: India's largest interactive science center with over 500 hands-on science exhibits and 3D science shows.
Mumbai.bestThing: Playing with interactive hands-on physics and space exhibits.

Mumbai.name: Global Vipassana Pagoda
Mumbai.blurb: A massive meditation dome monument near Gorai inspired by Myanmar's Shwedagon Pagoda, holding Buddha relics.
Mumbai.bestThing: Standing inside the world's largest stone dome built without pillars.
Mumbai.nearTransport: Ferry from Gorai Creek / Borivali Station

Mumbai.name: Girgaon Chowpatty
Mumbai.blurb: A famous public beach at the northern end of Marine Drive, iconic for Ganesh Visarjan immersion ceremonies.
Mumbai.bestThing: Eating authentic Mumbai Bhel Puri and Kulfi Falooda by the beach.

Mumbai.name: Babulnath Temple
Mumbai.blurb: An ancient Shiva temple situated on a hillock near Girgaon Chowpatty, dating back to 1780.
Mumbai.bestThing: Riding the hill elevator or walking stone stairs to the elevated shrine.

Mumbai.name: Worli Sea Face
Mumbai.blurb: A scenic coastal promenade in South-Central Mumbai known for high ocean waves during monsoon season.
Mumbai.bestThing: Watching monsoon ocean waves crash over sea wall barriers.

Bengaluru.name: Cubbon Park
Bengaluru.blurb: A 300-acre historic park in the heart of Bengaluru created in 1870, home to over 6,000 trees and red brick heritage buildings.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Walking amidst bamboo groves and colonial red brick High Court building.

Bengaluru.name: Lalbagh Botanical Garden
Bengaluru.blurb: A 240-acre botanical garden commissioned by Hyder Ali in 1760, featuring a famous glasshouse inspired by London's Crystal Palace.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Visiting the 1890 Glass House and 3-billion-year-old Lalbagh Rock.

Bengaluru.name: Bangalore Palace
Bengaluru.blurb: A Tudor-style royal palace built in 1887 by King Chamarajendra Wadiyar X, inspired by England's Windsor Castle.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Exploring wood-carved interiors, vintage photos, and royal ballroom.
Bengaluru.nearTransport: Cantonment Railway Station / Cubbon Park Metro

Bengaluru.name: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace
Bengaluru.blurb: Completed in 1791, an ornate teakwood palace built by Tipu Sultan featuring carved pillars, arches, and balconies.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Admiring two-story teak pillars with intricate floral mortar paintings.

Bengaluru.name: ISKCON Temple Bangalore
Bengaluru.blurb: One of the world's largest ISKCON temple complexes, opened in 1997 on Hare Krishna Hill featuring modern glass architecture.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Ascending the hilltop temple and tasting delicious prasadam.

Bengaluru.name: Vidhana Soudha
Bengaluru.blurb: Built in 1956 in Neo-Dravidian architecture, it is the seat of Karnataka's state legislature and an iconic landmark.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Photographing the illuminated grand stone facade on Sunday evenings.

Bengaluru.name: Bull Temple
Bengaluru.blurb: A 16th-century temple built by Kempe Gowda I housing a monolithic granite deity of Nandi the sacred bull.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Viewing the gigantic 4.5-meter tall carved monolithic Nandi bull.

Bengaluru.name: St. Mary's Basilica
Bengaluru.blurb: The oldest church in Bengaluru, built in 1882 in Gothic revival architecture with stained glass windows.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Admiring intricate French-designed stained glass windows.
Bengaluru.nearTransport: MG Road Metro / Cubbon Park Metro

Bengaluru.name: HAL Aerospace Museum
Bengaluru.blurb: India's first aviation museum established in 2001, exhibiting vintage aircraft, jet engines, and flight simulators.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Seeing actual historic fighter jets and testing real flight simulators.

Bengaluru.name: Visvesvaraya Industrial & Technological Museum
Bengaluru.blurb: Established in 1962 in memory of Sir M. Visvesvaraya, featuring interactive halls on engine technology and space.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Interacting with hands-on engine gear models and Wright Brothers replica.

Bengaluru.name: Government Museum & Venkatappa Art Gallery
Bengaluru.blurb: Established in 1866, it is one of the oldest museums in India, exhibiting ancient Kannada inscriptions and coins.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Seeing the 450 AD Halmidi inscription, the oldest written Kannada record.

Bengaluru.name: Gavi Gangadhareshwara Temple
Bengaluru.blurb: A 9th-century rock-cut cave temple famous for monolith stone discs and solar alignment during Makar Sankranti.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Exploring ancient natural stone cave passages holding Shiva shrines.

Bengaluru.name: Jawaharlal Nehru Planetarium
Bengaluru.blurb: Established in 1989, offering sky theater shows, science parks, and astronomy exhibits for all ages.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Watching fulldome digital space projection shows in the planetarium.
Bengaluru.nearTransport: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Metro / Vidhana Soudha Metro

Bengaluru.name: Sankey Tank
Bengaluru.blurb: A man-made lake built in 1875 by Richard Hieram Sankey to meet Bengaluru's water supply needs, surrounded by gardens.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Walking the paved lakeside track surrounded by old trees and birds.

Bengaluru.name: Ulsoor Lake
Bengaluru.blurb: One of the largest lakes in Bengaluru, constructed by Kempe Gowda II in the 16th century with several islands.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Relaxing along the tree-lined shoreline watching boats on the lake.

Bengaluru.name: Commercial Street
Bengaluru.blurb: A legendary shopping hub famous for clothing, footwear, jewelry, and bustling bazaar lanes.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Exploring narrow lanes for colorful street fashion and silver trinkets.

Bengaluru.name: National Gallery of Modern Art
Bengaluru.blurb: Set inside a restored 100-year-old colonial mansion surrounded by gardens, displaying modern Indian art.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Enjoying art exhibits inside a peaceful heritage garden mansion.

Bengaluru.name: Bannerghatta Biological Park
Bengaluru.blurb: A 260-sq-km national park featuring a zoo, butterfly park, and tiger-lion jungle safari 22 km south of Bengaluru.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Riding the protected jungle bus safari to see lions and tigers.

Bengaluru.name: VV Puram Food Street
Bengaluru.blurb: Bengaluru's famous vegetarian food street offering local delicacies like Dosa, Holige, and Akki Roti.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Tasting piping hot Ghee Masala Dosa and Holige from street stalls.

Bengaluru.name: Church Street
Bengaluru.blurb: A famous pedestrian-friendly granite-paved avenue lined with bookstores, cafes, art murals, and street performers.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Browsing vintage books at Blossom Book House and street music.

Bengaluru.name: Kote Venkataramana Temple
Bengaluru.blurb: A 1689 Dravidian Hindu temple built by King Chikka Devaraja Wodeyar adjoining Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Viewing ornate Vijayanagara-style stone pillars and Gopuram.

Bengaluru.name: Nandi Hills
Bengaluru.blurb: An ancient hill fortress 60 km north of Bengaluru at 1,478 meters altitude, famous for sunrise views above clouds.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Watching early morning sunrise over sea-of-clouds from hill cliff.

Bengaluru.name: Someshwara Temple Halasuru
Bengaluru.blurb: One of the oldest temples in Bengaluru, dating back to the Chola period with major additions by Kempe Gowda.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Inspecting Chola and Vijayanagara carved stone pillars.

Bengaluru.name: Freedom Park
Bengaluru.blurb: Located on the site of the former Central Jail built in 1867, transformed into a 21-acre public park and monument.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Walking through preserved historic prison watchtowers and barracks.

Bengaluru.name: Bangalore Fort
Bengaluru.blurb: Originally built as a mud fort in 1537 by Kempe Gowda I and converted into stone by Hyder Ali in 1761.
Bengaluru.bestThing: Viewing the preserved Delhi Gate stone bastion and carved arches.

Hyderabad.name: Charminar
Hyderabad.blurb: A 1591 mosque and monument built by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah with four 56-meter tall ornamental minarets.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Climbing to upper balcony arches framing Old City bazaar views.

Hyderabad.name: Golconda Fort
Hyderabad.blurb: A medieval fortress citadel built by the Qutb Shahi dynasty, famous for acoustics, palaces, and diamond vaults.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Experiencing the famous acoustic hand-clap echo from Fateh Darwaza to hilltop palace.

Hyderabad.name: Hussain Sagar Lake
Hyderabad.blurb: Built in 1563 by Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah, a heart-shaped lake featuring an 18-meter monolithic Buddha statue.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Taking a boat ride to the monolithic Buddha statue at center of the lake.

Hyderabad.name: Chowmahalla Palace
Hyderabad.blurb: The official palace seat of the Nizams of Hyderabad, built between 1750 and 1869, featuring grand courtyards.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Viewing 19 Belgian crystal chandeliers inside Khilwat Mubarak durbar hall.

Hyderabad.name: Qutb Shahi Tombs
Hyderabad.blurb: A landscaped heritage park containing domed mausoleums and mosques of the seven Qutb Shahi rulers.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Walking amidst magnificent domed stone tombs surrounded by gardens.

Hyderabad.name: Salar Jung Museum
Hyderabad.blurb: One of India's three National Museums, holding the personal collection of Salar Jung III with 43,000 artifacts.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Watching the famous 19th-century musical bracket clock strike every hour.

Hyderabad.name: Birla Mandir
Hyderabad.blurb: A Hindu temple built of 2,000 tons of pure white Rajasthani marble atop Naubat Pahad hill overlooking the lake.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Enjoying white marble carving art and hilltop views of Hussain Sagar Lake.

Hyderabad.name: Ramoji Film City
Hyderabad.blurb: Certified by Guinness World Records as the world's largest film studio complex, spanning 2,000 acres.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Touring live cinema sets, stunt shows, and thematic gardens.

Hyderabad.name: Mecca Masjid
Hyderabad.blurb: One of India's oldest and largest mosques, commissioned in 1614 with central arches built from bricks brought from Mecca.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Viewing the massive granite arches and historic Nizam royal tombs.

Hyderabad.name: Laad Bazaar
Hyderabad.blurb: A historic market operating since Qutb Shahi times, famous for traditional lacquer bangles and wedding jewelry.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Watching artisans hand-craft glittering glass and lacquer bangles.

Hyderabad.name: Falaknuma Palace
Hyderabad.blurb: Built in 1893 by Nawab Vikar-ul-Umra, a rare Italian marble palace that served as the Nizam's guest residence.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Marveling at the 101-seat dining table and Venetian chandeliers.

Hyderabad.name: Nehru Zoological Park
Hyderabad.blurb: A 380-acre zoo established in 1963, housing over 1,500 species of wild animals in natural enclosures.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Riding the safari bus to spot Asiatic lions and Bengal tigers.

Hyderabad.name: Lumbini Park
Hyderabad.blurb: A small urban park on the banks of Hussain Sagar Lake featuring laser shows, musical fountains, and boat rides.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Watching evening laser light shows dancing over water fountains.

Hyderabad.name: NTR Gardens
Hyderabad.blurb: A 34-acre urban park built in memory of N. T. Rama Rao, featuring toy train rides and giant machan structures.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Riding the mini toy train around landscaped gardens and fountains.

Hyderabad.name: Taramati Baradari
Hyderabad.blurb: A 17th-century music pavilion with 12 doorways built by Abdullah Qutb Shah for his legendary singer Taramati.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Ascending stone arches for views of Golconda Fort at sunset.

Hyderabad.name: Shilparamam
Hyderabad.blurb: An 65-acre arts and crafts village created in 1992 to preserve rural Indian crafts, folk dance, and handlooms.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Browsing traditional artisan stalls amidst ethnic rural cottages.

Hyderabad.name: Durgam Cheruvu & Cable Bridge
Hyderabad.blurb: A scenic freshwater lake featuring an iconic 233-meter cable-stayed bridge spanning across Madhapur and Jubilee Hills.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Walking the pedestrian cable bridge as multi-colored LED lights glow.

Hyderabad.name: Purani Haveli
Hyderabad.blurb: The official palace residence of the 5th Nizam, housing the famous Nizam's Museum and world's longest wooden wardrobe.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Viewing the 240-foot long hand-carved mahogany double-decker wardrobe.

Hyderabad.name: KBR National Park
Hyderabad.blurb: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy National Park covers 390 acres of urban forest habitat holding Chiran Palace and wild peacocks.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Walking the shaded outer jungle track with peacocks roaming freely.

Hyderabad.name: BM Birla Science Centre
Hyderabad.blurb: Features a modern planetarium, dinosaur museum with a 160-million-year-old Kotasaurus fossil, and interactive science halls.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Seeing the authentic 160-million-year-old Kotasaurus dinosaur skeleton.

Hyderabad.name: Telangana State Archaeology Museum
Hyderabad.blurb: Hyderabad's oldest museum located in Public Gardens, famous for its ancient Egyptian mummy dating back to 2500 BCE.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Viewing the 4,000-year-old Egyptian mummy of Princess Naishu.

Hyderabad.name: Peddamma Temple
Hyderabad.blurb: A popular Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Santhanam (Peddamma), attracting thousands during Bonalu festival.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Experiencing traditional floral Bonalu festival rituals and Gopuram.

Hyderabad.name: Chilkur Balaji Temple
Hyderabad.blurb: An ancient 500-year-old Venkateswara temple popularly known as 'Visa Balaji', famous for accepting no monetary donations.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Performing 11 pradakshinas around the shrine without VIP queues.

Hyderabad.name: Sanjeevaiah Park
Hyderabad.blurb: A 99-acre public park on the northern banks of Hussain Sagar Lake featuring a rose garden and national flag mast.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Viewing the 308-foot national flag mast standing over the lake.

Hyderabad.name: Spanish Mosque
Hyderabad.blurb: Built in 1906 by Nawab Viqar-ul-Umra in unique Moorish and Hispanic-Islamic architecture featuring spire minarets.
Hyderabad.bestThing: Admiring rare Moorish stone minarets reminiscent of Cordoba Cathedral.

Jaipur.name: Amber Fort
Jaipur.blurb: A majestic hilltop UNESCO fortress constructed in 1592 by Raja Man Singh I using red sandstone and marble.
Jaipur.bestThing: Marveling at the intricate convex glass mirror work in Sheesh Mahal.

Jaipur.name: Hawa Mahal
Jaipur.blurb: Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, a 5-story pink sandstone palace with 953 carved jharokha windows.
Jaipur.bestThing: Viewing the 953 honeycomb windows designed for royal women to observe street processions.

Jaipur.name: City Palace Jaipur
Jaipur.blurb: Established in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, a royal palace complex blending Rajput, Mughal, and European architecture.
Jaipur.bestThing: Admiring the Peacock Gate inside Pritam Niwas Chowk.

Jaipur.name: Jantar Mantar
Jaipur.blurb: A UNESCO World Heritage astronomical monument completed in 1734 by Sawai Jai Singh II, holding 19 stone instruments.
Jaipur.bestThing: Seeing Vrihat Samrat Yantra, the world's largest stone sundial measuring time to 2-second accuracy.

Jaipur.name: Nahargarh Fort
Jaipur.blurb: Built in 1734 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II atop Aravalli hills, offering sweeping sunset views of Jaipur.
Jaipur.bestThing: Watching sunset over the entire Pink City cityscape from stone battlements.

Jaipur.name: Jal Mahal
Jaipur.blurb: A 5-story red sandstone palace submerged in the center of Man Sagar Lake, renovated by Maharaja Jai Singh II.
Jaipur.bestThing: Photographing the glowing palace reflecting on lake waters at dusk.

Jaipur.name: Albert Hall Museum
Jaipur.blurb: The oldest museum in Rajasthan, built in 1887 in Indo-Saracenic style, showcasing carpet collections and Egyptian mummies.
Jaipur.bestThing: Viewing 16th-century Persian carpets and nighttime lit facade.

Jaipur.name: Jaigarh Fort
Jaipur.blurb: Built in 1726 by Jai Singh II to protect Amber Fort, holding Jaivana, the world's largest cannon on wheels.
Jaipur.bestThing: Inspecting the massive 50-ton Jaivana cannon resting on iron wheels.

Jaipur.name: Galtaji Temple
Jaipur.blurb: An ancient Hindu pilgrimage site in a narrow mountain pass, featuring natural holy water kunds and friendly monkeys.
Jaipur.bestThing: Exploring pink stone temple pavilions surrounding natural spring pools.

Jaipur.name: Panna Meena ka Kund
Jaipur.blurb: A 16th-century symmetrical geometric stepwell featuring crisscross stone staircases leading down to natural groundwater.
Jaipur.bestThing: Photographing the stunning symmetrical crisscross stone stairs.

Jaipur.name: Birla Mandir Jaipur
Jaipur.blurb: Also known as Laxmi Narayan Temple, a modern Hindu temple built in 1988 of pure white Rajasthani marble.
Jaipur.bestThing: Viewing intricate marble relief carvings depicting philosophers and gods.

Jaipur.name: Johari Bazaar
Jaipur.blurb: Jaipur's famous traditional bazaar known worldwide for handmade Kundan jewelry, precious gemstones, and sarees.
Jaipur.bestThing: Shopping for authentic Kundan jewelry and Rajasthani tie-dye fabrics.

Jaipur.name: Bapu Bazaar
Jaipur.blurb: A famous market located in the Pink City walls, popular for traditional Mojari leather shoes and block-print textiles.
Jaipur.bestThing: Bargaining for colorful camel leather Mojari shoes and block prints.

Jaipur.name: Sisodia Rani Garden
Jaipur.blurb: Built in 1728 for the queen of Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, featuring multi-tiered terraced gardens and fountains.
Jaipur.bestThing: Strolling multi-level terraced gardens decorated with Radha-Krishna murals.

Jaipur.name: Kanak Vrindavan
Jaipur.blurb: A manicured garden complex nestled in a valley below Nahargarh hill, resembling Vrindavan gardens.
Jaipur.bestThing: Walking past white marble fountains framed by Aravalli hill views.

Jaipur.name: Govind Dev Ji Temple
Jaipur.blurb: A sacred 1735 Hindu temple inside the City Palace complex holding the deity of Lord Krishna brought from Vrindavan.
Jaipur.bestThing: Participating in energetic morning Aarti prayers with local devotees.

Jaipur.name: Chokhi Dhani
Jaipur.blurb: A 5-star ethnic village resort depicting traditional Rajasthani rural culture, puppet shows, folk dance, and dining.
Jaipur.bestThing: Enjoying authentic Rajasthani Dal Baati Churma thali and Kalbelia dance.

Jaipur.name: Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing
Jaipur.blurb: Located in a restored 16th-century mansion near Amber Fort, dedicated to preserving hand block printing heritage.
Jaipur.bestThing: Trying hands-on wooden block printing on fabric with master artisans.

Jaipur.name: Patrika Gate
Jaipur.blurb: A vibrant multi-arched gate at Jawahar Circle garden, hand-painted with colorful murals depicting Rajasthani culture.
Jaipur.bestThing: Walking through hand-painted colorful archways depicting Rajasthan history.

Jaipur.name: Jawahar Circle Garden
Jaipur.blurb: Claimed to be the largest circular park in Asia, featuring jogging tracks, musical fountains, and Patrika Gate.
Jaipur.bestThing: Watching the evening musical water fountain show.

Jaipur.name: Central Park Jaipur
Jaipur.blurb: Jaipur's largest public park created by the Jaipur Development Authority, featuring a 5-km running track and 206-ft flag mast.
Jaipur.bestThing: Jogging along lush green lawns beside India's 206-foot national flag.

Jaipur.name: Maharani Ki Chhatriyan
Jaipur.blurb: The funeral site holding exquisite carved marble cenotaphs of royal women of the Jaipur royal family.
Jaipur.bestThing: Admiring intricately carved white marble domes and cenotaph pillars.

Jaipur.name: Gaitore ki Chhatriyan
Jaipur.blurb: The royal crematorium ground for the Kachwaha Rajput kings, featuring delicately carved marble chhatris.
Jaipur.bestThing: Viewing the magnificent carved marble cenotaph of Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II.

Jaipur.name: MI Road
Jaipur.blurb: Jaipur's main arterial shopping avenue lined with heritage shops, brassware stores, and iconic lassi shops.
Jaipur.bestThing: Drinking thick creamy kulhad lassi at legendary Lassiwala (est. 1944).

Jaipur.name: Chandpole Gate
Jaipur.blurb: One of the seven historic high gates built into the Pink City wall in 1727, marking the western city entrance.
Jaipur.bestThing: Photographing the historic pink arched city gate during golden hour.

Varanasi.name: Dashashwamedh Ghat
Varanasi.blurb: The main and most historic ghat on the Ganges River in Varanasi, world-famous for its daily evening Ganga Aarti ceremony.
Varanasi.bestThing: Watching priests perform the grand Ganga Aarti with brass lamps at dusk.

Varanasi.name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
Varanasi.blurb: One of the twelve sacred Jyotirlinga Shiva temples, rebuilt by Ahilyabai Holkar in 1780 with a 15.5-meter golden spire.
Varanasi.bestThing: Experiencing the spiritual energy and golden spire inside Kashi Vishwanath Corridor.

Varanasi.name: Sarnath Sacred Site
Varanasi.blurb: Located 10 km northeast of Varanasi, where Lord Buddha gave his first sermon after attaining enlightenment.
Varanasi.bestThing: Standing before the massive 43.6-meter Dhamek Stupa built by Emperor Ashoka.

Varanasi.name: Manikarnika Ghat
Varanasi.blurb: The principal sacred cremation ghat on the Ganges, where funeral pyres burn continuously 24 hours a day.
Varanasi.bestThing: Observing sacred funeral traditions and ancient Manikarnika Kund.

Varanasi.name: Assi Ghat
Varanasi.blurb: The southernmost major ghat where the Assi River meets the Ganges, famous for morning Subah-e-Banaras concerts and yoga.
Varanasi.bestThing: Experiencing morning Subah-e-Banaras classical music and sunrise yoga.

Varanasi.name: Sarnath Archaeological Museum
Varanasi.blurb: Established in 1910, housing the original Lion Capital of Ashoka (India's national emblem) carved in sandstone.
Varanasi.bestThing: Viewing the original 3rd-century BCE Lion Capital of Ashoka.

Varanasi.name: Banaras Hindu University
Varanasi.blurb: Founded in 1916 by Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, one of Asia's largest residential universities spanning 1,300 acres.
Varanasi.bestThing: Driving along tree-lined avenues to New Vishwanath Temple and Bharat Kala Bhavan.

Varanasi.name: New Vishwanath Temple
Varanasi.blurb: Located inside BHU campus, a 77-meter marble temple tower built by the Birla family, taller than Qutub Minar.
Varanasi.bestThing: Viewing Gita verses inscribed on internal marble walls of the towering shrine.

Varanasi.name: Ramnagar Fort
Varanasi.blurb: An 18th-century cream-colored sandstone fort on the eastern bank of the Ganges, ancestral home of the Kashi Naresh.
Varanasi.bestThing: Viewing royal vintage car collection, swords, and astronomical clocks.

Varanasi.name: Bharat Kala Bhavan
Varanasi.blurb: An university museum inside BHU established in 1920, exhibiting miniature paintings, sculptures, and textiles.
Varanasi.bestThing: Viewing rare Mughal miniature paintings and ancient palm-leaf manuscripts.

Varanasi.name: Tulsi Manas Mandir
Varanasi.blurb: A white marble temple built in 1964 where Goswami Tulsidas composed the epic Ramcharitmanas.
Varanasi.bestThing: Reading Ramcharitmanas verses engraved on marble walls across 2 floors.

Varanasi.name: Durga Kund Temple
Varanasi.blurb: An 18th-century red sandstone temple dedicated to Goddess Durga, adjoining a rectangular water tank (Kund).
Varanasi.bestThing: Admiring Nagara multi-tiered red stone spires framing Durga Kund tank.

Varanasi.name: Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple
Varanasi.blurb: Established by saint Goswami Tulsidas in the 16th century, dedicated to Lord Hanuman for removing troubles.
Varanasi.bestThing: Listening to evening Hanuman Chalisa chants and partaking in sweet Besan Ladoo.

Varanasi.name: Harishchandra Ghat
Varanasi.blurb: One of the two ancient cremation ghats, named after King Harishchandra who worked here for truth and virtue.
Varanasi.bestThing: Observing historic riverfront stone steps and ancient rituals.

Varanasi.name: Scindia Ghat
Varanasi.blurb: Famous for its partially submerged Shiva temple which collapsed into the Ganges riverbed under its own weight in 1830.
Varanasi.bestThing: Photographing the partially submerged stone temple leaning in river waters.

Varanasi.name: Darbhanga Ghat
Varanasi.blurb: Features a majestic 1812 sandstone palace built by the royal family of Bihar, now restored into a heritage hotel.
Varanasi.bestThing: Marveling at the carved Greek pillar balcony framing the Ganges.

Varanasi.name: Chet Singh Ghat
Varanasi.blurb: A fortified 18th-century stone riverfront fortress ghat where Maharaja Chet Singh fought Warren Hastings in 1781.
Varanasi.bestThing: Viewing the massive stone fort bastions rising straight out of the Ganges.

Varanasi.name: Panchganga Ghat
Varanasi.blurb: The sacred confluence where five mythical rivers meet, crowned by Emperor Aurangzeb's Alamgir Mosque.
Varanasi.bestThing: Viewing Alamgir Mosque soaring high above steep riverfront stone stairs.

Varanasi.name: Kedar Ghat
Varanasi.blurb: Distinctive for its red-and-white striped steps leading to Ketareshwar Shiva Temple, built in South Indian style.
Varanasi.bestThing: Walking the bold red-and-white painted stone steps down to the river.

Varanasi.name: Bharat Mata Mandir
Varanasi.blurb: Inaugurated by Mahatma Gandhi in 1936, housing a relief map of undivided India carved out of marble.
Varanasi.bestThing: Viewing the 3D relief topographical map of India carved in marble.

Varanasi.name: Godowlia Market
Varanasi.blurb: Varanasi's busiest traditional market near Dashashwamedh Ghat, famous for Banarasi silk sarees and brassware.
Varanasi.bestThing: Shopping for hand-woven Banarasi silk brocade sarees and wooden toys.

Varanasi.name: Chaukhandi Stupa
Varanasi.blurb: A 5th-century Gupta-era terraced brick stupa in Sarnath, modified in 1588 with an octagonal tower by Govardhan.
Varanasi.bestThing: Climbing the green mound to view the 16th-century Mughal octagonal tower.

Varanasi.name: Thai Temple Sarnath
Varanasi.blurb: A serene monastery built in traditional Thai architecture, housing an 80-foot standing Buddha statue in gardens.
Varanasi.bestThing: Viewing the 80-foot standing golden-colored Buddha statue amidst lotus gardens.

Varanasi.name: Tibetan Temple Sarnath
Varanasi.blurb: Built in 1955, a traditional Tibetan Buddhist monastery housing a statue of Shakyamuni Buddha and prayer wheels.
Varanasi.bestThing: Spinning brass Tibetan prayer wheels along the peaceful courtyard.

Varanasi.name: Shri Satyanarayan Tulsi Manas Temple
Varanasi.blurb: Adjoining Tulsi Manas Mandir, featuring manicured gardens depicting scenes from the Ramayana with mechanical statues.
Varanasi.bestThing: Viewing animated mechanical puppet displays of Ramayana epics.

Kochi.name: Veeranpuzha
Kochi.blurb: Veeranpuzha is a northern extension of Vembanad Lake in Kochi, famous for Pokkali rice-fish farming wetlands.
Kochi.bestThing: Boating through Pokkali wetland backwaters and watching bird life.

Kochi.name: Indo-Portuguese Museum
Kochi.blurb: Located in the compound of the Bishop's House in Fort Kochi, showcasing Portuguese Christian art and artifacts.
Kochi.bestThing: Viewing 16th-century teak altarpieces and silver processional crosses.

Kochi.name: Kerala Folklore Museum
Kochi.blurb: A 3-story architectural marvel constructed from wood and stone holding 4,000 folklore and dance artifacts.
Kochi.bestThing: Exploring 4,000 authentic Theyyam masks, costumes, and ancient weapons.

Kochi.name: Kochi-Muziris Biennale
Kochi.blurb: India's largest contemporary international art exhibition held across heritage sea warehouses in Fort Kochi.
Kochi.bestThing: Viewing contemporary installation art inside 19th-century pepper warehouses.

Kochi.name: Thrikkakara Temple
Kochi.blurb: An ancient Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Vamana, central to the origin story of Kerala's Onam festival.
Kochi.bestThing: Experiencing the spiritual center of Onam celebrations and Kerala murals.

Kochi.name: Chinese Fishing Nets
Kochi.blurb: Fixed shore-operated cantilever fishing structures introduced by Chinese traders in the 14th century.
Kochi.bestThing: Helping fishermen lift giant wooden cantilever nets against sunset skies.

Kochi.name: Mattancherry Palace
Kochi.blurb: Built by the Portuguese in 1555 and presented to the King of Cochin, famed for 16th-century Ramayana mural paintings.
Kochi.bestThing: Viewing detailed 16th-century royal bedroom murals painted in tempera.

Kochi.name: Fort Kochi Beach
Kochi.blurb: A scenic historic beach promenade framed by giant rain trees, colonial bungalows, and sea cargo views.
Kochi.bestThing: Strolling the beach walkway at dusk past cargo ships entering Kochi port.

Kochi.name: Paradesi Synagogue
Kochi.blurb: Built in 1568 by Sephardic Jewish immigrants, it is the oldest active synagogue in the Commonwealth of Nations.
Kochi.bestThing: Viewing hand-painted 18th-century Chinese porcelain floor tiles and Belgian glass chandeliers.

Kochi.name: Jew Town Bazaar
Kochi.blurb: A famous antique shopping street leading to the Paradesi Synagogue, packed with spice stores and carved furniture.
Kochi.bestThing: Shopping for spices, antique carved wooden doors, and vintage brassware.

Kochi.name: St. Francis Church
Kochi.blurb: Built by Portuguese Franciscans in 1503, it is the oldest European-built church in India where Vasco da Gama was buried.
Kochi.bestThing: Standing before the original tombstone of Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama.

Kochi.name: Santa Cruz Cathedral Basilica
Kochi.blurb: One of eight basilicas in Kerala, built by Portuguese in 1505 featuring Gothic spires and ceiling frescoes.
Kochi.bestThing: Admiring ceiling frescoes depicting 'The Last Supper' painted in Italian style.

Kochi.name: Marine Drive Kochi
Kochi.blurb: A popular waterfront promenade facing the backwaters of Kochi, featuring Rainbow Bridge and boat jetties.
Kochi.bestThing: Walking Rainbow Bridge at night watching harbor vessel lights.

Kochi.name: Bolgatty Palace & Island
Kochi.blurb: A Dutch palace built in 1744 on Bolgatty Island by Dutch traders, surrounded by golf greens and backwaters.
Kochi.bestThing: Walking the island heritage lawns overlooking Kochi container port.

Kochi.name: Willingdon Island
Kochi.blurb: A man-made island created in 1936 by Lord Willingdon from dredged backwater soil, seat of Southern Naval Command.
Kochi.bestThing: Watching naval ships and international cargo liners enter port.

Kochi.name: Mangalavanam Bird Sanctuary
Kochi.blurb: A 2.74-hectare mangrove forest sanctuary in central Ernakulam, known as the green lungs of Kochi.
Kochi.bestThing: Spotting migratory waterbirds inside lush urban mangrove woods.

Kochi.name: Cherai Beach
Kochi.blurb: A 10-km sandy beach on Vypin Island where calm sea waters meet serene backwater lagoons.
Kochi.bestThing: Walking seashell-lined sands where sea and backwaters run side-by-side.

Kochi.name: Hill Palace Museum
Kochi.blurb: Built in 1865, Kerala's largest archaeological museum spanning 54 acres with 49 traditional buildings.
Kochi.bestThing: Viewing the 1.7-kg 200-diamond golden crown of Cochin Maharajas.

Kochi.name: Subhash Bose Park
Kochi.blurb: A 12-acre waterfront park facing Vembanad Lake in central Ernakulam, featuring paved walkways and musical fountains.
Kochi.bestThing: Relaxing on lakeside benches watching evening ferry boat crossings.

Kochi.name: Ernakulam Shiva Temple
Kochi.blurb: A major ancient Hindu temple in Ernakulam city center dedicated to Shiva as Ernakulathappan.
Kochi.bestThing: Experiencing classic Kerala temple architecture and Panchavadyam drumming.

Kochi.name: Chottanikkara Bhagavathy Temple
Kochi.blurb: A famous Mother Goddess temple where the deity is worshipped as Saraswati in morning, Bhadrakali at noon, and Lakshmi in evening.
Kochi.bestThing: Experiencing powerful evening Guruthi pujas inside the sacred lower shrine.

Kochi.name: Museum of Kerala History
Kochi.blurb: Founded by R. Madhavan Nayar, featuring light-and-sound shows depicting 2,000 years of Kerala history through life-size statues.
Kochi.bestThing: Watching the animated light and sound historical diorama show.

Kochi.name: Vypin Island & Lighthouse
Kochi.blurb: A 27-km long barrier island holding the 46-meter high Puthuvype Lighthouse offering ocean views.
Kochi.bestThing: Climbing Puthuvype Lighthouse for panoramic views of the Arabian Sea.

Kochi.name: Aspinwall House
Kochi.blurb: A 19th-century seafront trading property established by John Aspinwall in 1867 for timber, pepper, and coconut oil.
Kochi.bestThing: Walking long historic wooden sea-facing verandahs.

Kochi.name: Sree Poornathrayeesa Temple
Kochi.blurb: The ancestral temple of the Royal Family of Cochin, dedicated to Lord Vishnu resting on Anantha.
Kochi.bestThing: Viewing traditional gold-gilded temple structures and elephant festival processions.
